text: Twenty videos ago, Fernbridge had a day-stale manual CSV export and a support desk that couldn't answer where a package actually was. This is the honest ending -- not a highlight reel.

What got built is real: scanners and GPS trackers into Kafka, a Databricks medallion lakehouse resolving one current status per package, and two purpose-built Fabric surfaces -- plus a real bug that was found, root-caused, and fixed with a permanent regression test.

What's still open, named plainly: no alerting beyond CI, a real possibility that batch and real-time briefly disagree during a backfill, and the scanners and Kafka itself remaining the one point this platform can't protect on its own.

This solved the real problems Renata and Devon brought to that first meeting, and found a real bug along the way. It didn't solve production monitoring or the fleet's own reliability -- those are named, not hidden.
Fernbridge now has what it never had: real history, and a real answer to where's my package, right now. That's the series.
